basics.description: Deploy a Microsoft Planetary Computer Pro **GeoCatalog** plus optional components: sample-data storage, an Azure OpenAI (Microsoft Foundry) agent, the Microsoft Aurora weather model on a GPU Foundry endpoint, and the **OneGrid web app** (Fabric plane + chat/report Container App). The GeoCatalog is always deployed; choose the rest. [Learn more](https://github.com/paulshaheen/OneGrid).

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: GeoCatalog is available in these regions during Preview.

basics.name: geoCatalogName
basics.label: GeoCatalog name
basics.toolTip: Lowercase letters and numbers, 3-24 characters. Leave blank to auto-generate a unique name.

options.text: The GeoCatalog is always deployed. Select any additional components below, then configure them on the following tabs.

elements.name: selected
elements.label: Optional components to deploy
elements.toolTip: Select one or more components. Use Select all for the complete environment.

allowedValues.label: Sample storage + ingestion identity
allowedValues.description: Storage account and managed identity for the bring-your-own-data ingestion path.

allowedValues.label: AI agent (Azure OpenAI / Foundry)
allowedValues.description: Azure OpenAI account + GPT deployment for agentic / reasoning GeoAI scenarios.

allowedValues.label: Aurora weather model (GPU Foundry endpoint)
allowedValues.description: Foundry (Azure ML) workspace + GPU managed-compute endpoint for the Microsoft Aurora model. Requires A100 GPU quota + marketplace terms.

allowedValues.label: Aurora scheduled forecast job (Container Apps)
allowedValues.description: Azure Container Apps Job that runs the Aurora forecast pipeline every 6 hours and publishes weather-events.json, keeping the map live without manual runs. Requires the Aurora weather model + sample storage, plus a prebuilt pipeline image.

allowedValues.label: OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)
allowedValues.description: Provisions OneGrid's Microsoft Fabric operational plane in-template: a Fabric workspace, lakehouse, eventhouse/KQL database, the geo_point_in_polygon hazard join + composite-risk tables, and (when a connection id is supplied) a OneLake shortcut to the model-outputs container. Runs OneGrid deploy.ps1 headless from the deployment as a user-assigned identity. Requires sample storage and an existing Fabric capacity.

allowedValues.label: OneGrid web app (AI Foundry + chat/report)
allowedValues.description: Stands up the OneGrid web application into this resource group: the AI Foundry account (reused from the AI agent when selected) and the chat/report Container App (built from source via ACR). Requires the OneGrid Fabric plane. The Fabric-plane identity is granted Owner on THIS resource group so the provisioner can create the resources and assign the app's data-plane roles.

allowedValues.label: OneGrid historical data seed (large)
allowedValues.description: Seeds the full OneGrid historical demo dataset into the lakehouse/eventhouse, cloud-seeded from the public release bundle (hundreds of MB, adds deployment time). Off by default. Requires the OneGrid Fabric plane.

options.text: No AI components are selected. These settings are ignored.

elements.name: openAiDeploymentName
elements.label: Model deployment name
elements.toolTip: Name of the Azure OpenAI model deployment.

constraints.validationMessage: Use 2-64 characters: letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore.

options.text: Aurora runs on a GPU managed-compute endpoint (Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4). The Foundry workspace + endpoint always deploy; the GPU model only deploys when you supply a model asset ID and have A100 quota + accepted marketplace terms.

elements.name: auroraInstanceType
elements.label: GPU instance type
elements.toolTip: GPU VM size for the Aurora managed-compute deployment. You must have quota for it in the selected region.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid VM size, e.g. Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4.

elements.name: createAuroraModelDeployment
elements.label: Deploy the Aurora model for me (official published asset)
elements.toolTip: Deploy the Aurora model onto the GPU endpoint using the official published asset (azureml://registries/azureml/models/Aurora/versions/4). Requires A100 quota in the region and accepted Azure Marketplace terms for Aurora. Leave unchecked to provision the workspace + endpoint only, or paste a specific asset ID below.

elements.name: auroraModelAssetId
elements.label: Aurora model asset ID (optional)
elements.toolTip: Registry model asset. The official storm-impact app uses azureml://registries/azureml/models/Aurora/versions/4. Leave blank to provision the workspace + endpoint only and deploy the model from the portal.

options.text: Runs the Aurora pipeline as a scheduled Container Apps Job so the map stays live without manual runs. The template provisions a dedicated Azure Container Registry and grants the job pull access automatically — you don't manage a registry. It needs the Aurora weather model (the GPU endpoint) and sample storage selected too. After deploying, build the image into the registry once (the exact command is in the deployment outputs, auroraImageBuildCommand): az acr build -r <registry> -t aurora-pipeline:latest aurora.
Also select 'Aurora weather model' and 'Sample storage' above — the scheduled job calls the GPU endpoint and publishes to the sample storage account, so it will not deploy without them.

elements.name: auroraJobImage
elements.label: Custom pipeline image (optional override)
elements.toolTip: Leave blank to use the Azure Container Registry this template provisions. Set this only to bring your own prebuilt image, e.g. myregistry.azurecr.io/aurora-pipeline:latest.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter an image reference like myregistry.azurecr.io/aurora-pipeline:latest, or leave blank to use the provisioned registry.

elements.name: auroraJobCron
elements.label: Schedule (cron, UTC)
elements.toolTip: Cron expression (UTC) for the forecast cadence. The default runs ~1 h after each synoptic cycle (00/06/12/18 UTC) to allow for input-data latency.

options.text: The OneGrid Fabric plane is not selected. These settings are ignored.

The OneGrid Fabric plane is provisioned in-template: during deployment, OneGrid deploy.ps1 runs headless as a user-assigned identity to create the Fabric workspace, lakehouse, eventhouse/KQL database, the geo_point_in_polygon hazard join, and (with a connection id) the OneLake shortcut to model-outputs. Prerequisites: the Fabric tenant setting 'Service principals can create workspaces, connections, and deployment pipelines' must be ON. A Fabric workspace cannot be created without a capacity: either let the template create a new F-SKU capacity below, or supply an existing capacity (F-SKU or Trial) that the deployment identity administers. If 'OneGrid web app' is also selected, the AI Foundry account and chat/report Container App are created in this resource group too.
Also select 'Sample storage + ingestion identity' above. The Fabric plane reads the model-outputs container in that storage account, so the seam will not deploy without it.

elements.name: createFabricCapacity
elements.label: Create a new Fabric capacity for me
elements.toolTip: When checked, the template provisions a new Microsoft Fabric F-SKU capacity in this resource group and deploys onto it — no existing capacity needed. Note: an F-SKU is billed hourly until you pause or delete it. Leave unchecked to reuse an existing capacity below.

elements.name: fabricCapacitySku
elements.label: New Fabric capacity SKU
elements.toolTip: SKU for the capacity the template creates. F2 is the smallest and cheapest; scale up for heavier workloads.

elements.name: fabricCapacityAdmin
elements.label: Capacity admin (email or object id, optional)
elements.toolTip: A user principal name (email) or Entra object id to add as an administrator of the new capacity so you can manage it in the Fabric portal. The deployment identity is always an admin. Leave blank to have only the deployment identity administer it.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter an email (user@contoso.com), an Entra object id GUID, or leave blank.

elements.name: fabricCapacityId
elements.label: Existing Fabric capacity (resource ID or GUID)
elements.toolTip: An existing Microsoft Fabric capacity (F-SKU or Trial). Paste the capacity resource ID (/subscriptions/.../providers/Microsoft.Fabric/capacities/<name>) or its GUID. Required when the Fabric plane is selected and you are not creating a new capacity.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a Fabric capacity GUID or its full resource ID.

elements.name: fabricWorkspaceName
elements.label: Fabric workspace name
elements.toolTip: Name for the Microsoft Fabric workspace that the OneGrid deploy will create on the capacity above.

constraints.validationMessage: Use 1-64 characters: letters, numbers, space, dash or underscore.

elements.name: createFabricConnection
elements.label: Create the storage connection for me (workspace identity)
elements.toolTip: Have the deployment create the Fabric cloud connection to the sample storage account for you using the Fabric workspace identity (secret-free). Leave checked to skip pasting a connection GUID.

elements.name: fabricConnectionId
elements.label: Fabric storage connection ID (optional)
elements.toolTip: GUID of an existing Fabric cloud connection to the sample storage account. Used only if you did not check 'Create the storage connection for me'. Leave blank to provision the workspace, lakehouse, eventhouse and hazard join now and add the shortcut later.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a connection GUID, e.g. 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, or leave blank.
